playbooks.title: Company Briefing
playbooks.when: On demand, before the meeting it is for.
playbooks.summary: Get a one-page briefing on a company, product, or person before a meeting, with a source and date for every fact.
playbooks.delivers: One page: what it is, the basics, who leads it, what it sells, recent changes, what's coming, and what isn't known. For a person: current roles, connections, and what they've said in public.

inputs.name: COMPANY
inputs.description: Company, product or person to brief on

inputs.name: PURPOSE
inputs.description: What the briefing is for

examples: What does Northwind do? I have a call with them in an hour.
Give me a one-pager on Globex before the partnership meeting.
Quick background on Initech's CEO.
Brief me on Northwind - what do they do, how big are they, who backs them?
This company came up in the board deck. What should I know about them?
What's new with Northwind?
Any recent news on Initech? What changed there lately?
playbooks.playbook:
Brief me on {COMPANY}. It is for: {PURPOSE}.

Use the LMTY MCP tools. Its public profiles need no sign-in. If the tools are not available, say so and stop: the server is `https://mcp.lmty.com/mcp`.

1. Call search_profiles for "{COMPANY}". A company, its product and its people are separate profiles. If several match and I have not said which, ask. If none match, pass on the tool's hint and stop.
2. Call get_profile for the match. The overview is the default; read `counts` to see which sections hold anything.
3. Make at most 4 more reads, chosen by the purpose: the `changes` section for what moved, get_connections for founders, leaders, investors and partners, the `statements` section for what its leaders said, get_calendar for what is coming and what happened lately: both sit at the end of its list, so read from an `offset` near `total` when the first call does not return everything. If an answer names `sectionsLeft`, ask for those next. A further page of a section you are already reading is not a new read: read it to its end, or say how many entries you read and how many the record counts.
4. Write one page:
   - What it is: 3 or 4 plain sentences, from official and reported statements only
   - The basics: founded, based, headcount, funding, each with grade, date and source
   - People: who founded and leads it, and up to 3 quotes from its leaders with venue and date
   - What it sells: plans and listed prices, how many customers are known by name, and the company's own count if it states one
   - What moved: 3 to 6 dated items, newest first. A change marked `found` is first seen, not news; use only added, removed and returned. Word a calendar or timeline entry's date by its basis: published is "reported on", observed is "seen on". An entry saying what a page no longer lists or now lists is not something that happened: one line at most, as "no longer listed as of" or "now lists"
   - What is coming, with dates
   - Not observed: every empty section
   - Sources: address, publisher, date
   For a person, People is their current roles, career in order, what they founded or backed, and what they said in public.
5. If I ask only what is new with {COMPANY}, skip steps 3 and 4. Read get_calendar and the `timeline` section, newest first, back 90 days. Write one screen: "read N of M entries, back to [date]"; at most 8 entries dated occurred or published, each with date, grade and source, or "Nothing dated on LMTY's record for {COMPANY} since [date]"; apart, as counts and never as news, what LMTY only first saw (observed, and page readings); one line for what was not read.

Rules: Keep every statement's grade: official means someone who speaks for one of the parties said it (check which party), reported means press or two independent sources, chatter means one unverified source and is never stated as fact. Give each fact the date it was last seen and its source address. An empty section is "not observed", never "none". A page can hold fewer entries than the limit asked for: read until `more` is empty. No motive, no prediction, and no adjective the sources did not use. If the profile is thin, write a short briefing and a long "Not observed" list. Answer from LMTY's record. Anything from outside it (a web search, a page you fetch, the company's site read directly) goes only in a last section headed "From the assistant's own web search", with its link and the date read: never in the page above it, and never in place of a figure on the record. Search only for what my purpose needs and the record lacks, and say what you searched for.

playbooks.title: Claim Check
playbooks.when: On demand, once per claim.
playbooks.summary: Check a claim about a company: who's making it, since when, and whether the evidence holds up.
playbooks.delivers: The claim restated so it can be tested, one of eight fixed verdicts (such as Supported, Unverified, or Out of date), who says so, the gap between claim and evidence, and what would settle it.

inputs.name: CLAIM
inputs.description: The exact wording of the claim

inputs.name: COMPANY
inputs.description: Who the claim is about

examples: Northwind's deck says they have 10,000 customers. Is that true?
Northwind says it's trusted by half of the largest banks. Is that real?
Did Initech really raise a $50M Series B?
Is Northwind actually SOC 2 certified?
A rep told the buyer Globex uses Northwind. Do they?
The assistant said Northwind has 800 employees. Where does that come from?
Someone posted that Acme's Pro plan is $50 a seat. That's wrong. Can you correct it?
playbooks.playbook:
Check this claim about {COMPANY}: "{CLAIM}".

Use the LMTY MCP tools. Its public profiles need no sign-in. If the tools are not available, say so and stop: the server is `https://mcp.lmty.com/mcp`.

1. Restate the claim so it can be tested: who, what, how much, as of when. Split a compound claim into its parts. Keep the original words beside your restatement, and say what you assumed.
2. Call search_profiles for "{COMPANY}" and for any second party the claim names, such as a customer, a partner or an investor. The second party's side is often the better evidence.
3. Read where this kind of claim lives: get_profile for the overview, the `facts` section narrowed with factKinds, the `customers` or `pricing` section, or get_connections. Collect every statement that bears on the claim, not only the one that matches it.
4. For each statement note its grade, LMTY's confidence, and each source's publisher, tier and dates. A get_connections edge carries a source count, not its sources: do not say where a set of ties comes from, or that none has a source of a given kind, unless you read get_profile with sections ["connections"] for them. Then ask: is the only voice the subject itself?
5. Give exactly one of these eight verdicts, worded as here, and one sentence of reasons naming sources and dates:
   Supported | The subject's own claim | Reported, not confirmed by the subject | Unverified | Disputed | Out of date | Not observed | Untestable
   Supported needs a source in a position to know (a register, a filing, the other party's own statement) or the subject plus an independent source; press alone is Reported. For a claim that one company uses another's product, the interested party is the vendor: write "The subject's own claim" as "The vendor's own claim". It is the same verdict, not a ninth.
6. State the gap: the unit ("customers" where the page says "users"), the scope, the tense, a rounder number. Two figures that count different things do not conflict; say what each counts.
7. Name the one or two things that would settle it: a filing, a register, the customer's own statement.
8. End with "Before repeating it": the form of the claim the evidence supports, attributed and dated.
9. If I ask you to correct the claim, draft 1 to 3 sentences only when the record holds an official, dated source on the same claim, plan and scope that says otherwise: quote it with its source and date, as a draft for a person to review. If not, write "No correction drafted" and which part failed, with no suggested response.

Rules: Keep every statement's grade: official means someone who speaks for one of the parties said it (check which party), reported means press or two independent sources, chatter means one unverified source and is never stated as fact. Give each fact the date it was last seen and its source address. An empty section is "not observed", never "none". A page can hold fewer entries than the limit asked for: read until `more` is empty. Never write "true" or "false"; the verdict describes the evidence. No word about anyone's motive: no "misleading", no "inflated". Nothing found is "Not observed", which is not evidence against the claim. Check the claim that was made, not a nearby one that is easier. The verdict comes from LMTY's record. Anything from outside it (a web search, a page you fetch, the company's site read directly) goes only in a last section headed "From the assistant's own web search", with its link and the date read: it never changes the verdict, and a claim the record does not hold stays "Not observed".

playbooks.title: Customer Map
playbooks.when: On demand. Monthly for a product being watched. A repeat run should lead with customer names added, removed, or listed again.
playbooks.summary: Find a product's publicly named customers by industry, company size, and country, and where each name comes from.
playbooks.delivers: The best-evidenced customers, how each is known, counts by segment, which customer names were added to or dropped from public lists, and what else they use.

inputs.name: PRODUCT
inputs.description: The product you want to see customers for

examples: Who uses Northwind?
Which industries does Northwind sell into?
Is Globex a Northwind customer?
Which logos has Initech lost this year?
How many customers do Northwind and Initech have in common?
playbooks.playbook:
Map the publicly named customers of {PRODUCT}.

Use the LMTY MCP tools. Its public profiles need no sign-in. If the tools are not available, say so and stop: the server is `https://mcp.lmty.com/mcp`.

1. Call search_profiles for "{PRODUCT}". Customers are recorded on the product's profile. If the company's profile shows none, read the product's before saying none are known.
2. Call get_profile for the overview. `counts.customers` is how many are publicly named. A count the company claims for itself is a fact of kind proof_point or financial: look in both before saying there is none. Report both numbers; neither corrects the other. A claimed figure stored as a bare value and label with no sentence is reported as stored, both in quotation marks, with its source and date: say the record does not hold its sentence, and do not complete it.
3. Call get_profile with sections ["customers"] and page with offset until `more` is empty or you have read 100. Say how many you read out of how many. If the count is 0 or there is no product profile, call get_connections with focusType and focusId of the product or company and kinds ["customer_of", "uses"], and report the ties that point at it as publicly named customers. Say they came from ties and carry no evidence kind, sector or size, and write "who makes the claim: not read".
4. For each customer you name, say who makes the claim and how it is known (`evidence`): the vendor ("Northwind names Globex as a customer on its customers page"), the customer itself (its own job ad or site), or a third party. A customer list is the vendor's own claim unless the customer or an independent source says so. Write "publicly named customers", never "its customers", "customers include" or "uses". `since` is a real start only when `sinceStated` is true; otherwise write "seen since".
5. Count the ones you read by sector, by size band and by country, with a row for "not given". Write "of the N read", never a share of all customers.
6. Report movement only where a source shows it: entries marked `ended`, and `alsoUses` entries with `moved` set. Two products for one customer is "recorded with both" unless the order of events is known. Give no reason for a removal unless a source states one.
7. Count which other products the same customers are recorded with (`alsoUses`). That entry does not say who makes the claim.

Write: The three numbers (claimed, publicly named, read) | Publicly named customers, best evidenced first (table, with who makes each claim) | How the claims are known | By sector, size, country | Movement | Other products the same customers are recorded with | What the publicly named set leaves out.

Rules: Keep every statement's grade: official means someone who speaks for one of the parties said it (check which party), reported means press or two independent sources, chatter means one unverified source and is never stated as fact. Give each fact the date it was last seen and its source address. An empty section is "not observed", never "none". A page can hold fewer entries than the limit asked for: read until `more` is empty. Known is a floor, not a total. A logo proves the vendor claims the customer, not that they still use it. A company missing from the list is "not observed as a customer", never "not a customer". Answer from LMTY's record. Anything from outside it (a web search, a fetched page) goes only in a last section, "From the assistant's own web search", with link and date read: never in the three numbers, the table or a count.

playbooks.title: Event Prep
playbooks.when: Weekly for a company being watched; on demand before a known date. A repeat run should lead with dates added, moved or passed.
playbooks.summary: Get ready for a company's upcoming launches, earnings calls, and events, based on what came up last time.
playbooks.delivers: A dated list of upcoming events. For each one: what's been announced, what came up the last few times, what to have ready, and two or three announcements to watch for.

inputs.name: COMPANY
inputs.description: The company with the upcoming event

inputs.name: ROLE
inputs.description: Who is preparing, such as sales, product, marketing, or leadership

examples: What does Northwind have coming up?
When is Northwind's next earnings call, and what did they say on the last one?
Northwind's conference is next month. What should we have ready?
Their new pricing takes effect on the 1st. Prep me.
Give me a watch list of Initech's dates for the quarter.
playbooks.playbook:
Prepare me for what {COMPANY} has coming up. I am preparing as: {ROLE}.

Use the LMTY MCP tools. Its public profiles need no sign-in. If the tools are not available, say so and stop: the server is `https://mcp.lmty.com/mcp`.

1. Call search_profiles for "{COMPANY}". A product's dates may sit with its maker, and a subsidiary's earnings with its listed parent; say whose calendar each date came from. Before saying whether there is a listed parent, read the ownership ties: get_connections with kinds ["subsidiary_of", "acquired"]. Otherwise write "parent not checked", never "no listed parent".
2. Call get_calendar with profileType, profileId and upcomingOnly true for what is coming, which sits at the end of the list. For the last 90 days, call it without upcomingOnly and read from an `offset` near `total`. A past entry's `startsAtBasis` says how its date is known: published is "reported on", observed is "seen on". An entry saying what a page no longer lists or now lists is not something that happened: give those in one line, as "no longer listed as of" or "now lists".
3. Call get_profile with sections ["occasions"] for its earnings calls and keynotes as read: tone, themes, and sentences of direction with quotes.
4. Something announced as coming with no date ("coming soon") gets no block: list it under "Announced without a date", with who said it and when. For each coming date write:
   - Stated: what a source says will happen, each line with its source
   - Expected: only a count of what past occasions of this kind carried, dated ("on 3 of the last 4 calls, pricing was discussed"), never what will be said. With fewer than 3 distinct occasions, say there are too few and quote what was said as precedent
   - Last time: the last 2 or 3 occasions of the same kind, with date, tone, themes and what was announced. How one landed: only from posts in get_profile sections ["chatter"] dated after it that name it, quoted and unverified. With none, write "no public reaction recorded"; never from memory or from the announcement itself
   - Prep: what to have current before, who watches on the day, what to check within a day after
   - Tripwires: 2 or 3 specific statements that could trigger work, such as "a list price for the new tier"
   Write every prep and tripwire line as an option or a check I may choose ("Option: ...", "Worth checking: ..."), never as an instruction.
5. Note a rhythm only with 3 or more past occasions, as a count with dates. Several recordings of one call are one occasion: count occasions, not entries. A release note or changelog entry is not an occasion.

With no announced date, or no profile, leave the per-date blocks out and print no empty table. Do not open with "nothing": say no date is announced in LMTY's sources as of the read date, written out, which is not nothing planned.

If you have run this before for {COMPANY}, lead with dates that were added, moved or passed since then. An earlier run is one in this conversation or in memory your client provides, never one you search files for. With none, say this run is the baseline.

Rules: Keep every statement's grade; chatter means one unverified source and is never stated as fact. Give each fact the date it was last seen and its source address. An empty section is "not observed", never "none". An announced date is a fact; what will be said on it is not: write "the last three did", never "so they will". A date that passed with nothing recorded is "outcome not observed". Web finds go only in a last section, "From the assistant's own web search", with link and date.

playbooks.title: Hiring Signals
playbooks.when: Weekly for a company being watched; on demand otherwise. A repeat run should lead with the change in open roles and any leadership move.
playbooks.summary: Read a company's open roles and leadership changes, and what to check next.
playbooks.delivers: Open roles now and, where available, 30 and 90 days ago, the mix by function and country, key role titles, leadership changes, and up to three readings, each with what was seen and what to check next.

inputs.name: COMPANY
inputs.description: The company to research

examples: What is Northwind hiring for right now?
Is Initech growing or cutting?
Who has joined Northwind's leadership team this year?
Northwind just posted a bunch of sales roles in Germany. What does that tell us?
Where does Northwind hire its engineers from?
playbooks.playbook:
Tell me what {COMPANY}'s open roles and leadership changes show.

Use the LMTY MCP tools. Its public profiles need no sign-in. If the tools are not available, say so and stop: the server is `https://mcp.lmty.com/mcp`.

1. Call search_profiles for "{COMPANY}" and take the company's profile. Open roles are recorded on the company, not its products.
2. Call get_profile with sections ["overview", "hiring", "trends", "people"]. If the answer names `sectionsLeft`, ask for those next.
3. Before any number, say what was read and when: `hiring.source.kind` is `board` (the whole list), `careers_page` (what one page showed) or `linkedin` (a sample, with the real `total` beside it), and `readAt` is the date.
4. Give open roles now, 30 days ago and 90 days ago, and how many are new in the last 30 days. A null earlier count means the record does not reach back: write "no earlier count", never "unchanged". Then the counts by function and by country.
5. Quote 5 or 6 role titles exactly, the ones that name a product, a market, a language or a first hire in a function. Give a posted date only when the record has one; otherwise write "not given" and call no role "newest". Where no role has a posted date, write "roles observed as of" the read date.
6. Call get_connections with kinds ["founded", "leads", "board_member", "works_at"] and includeEnded true. List who leads it, and who joined or left with the date and how it is known. An edge's `since` may be when LMTY first saw the role: write "as of", not "joined" or "became", unless a stated start was read. The stated start and ended roles are on the works_at ties and in get_profile with sections ["connections"]. With no dated arrival or departure on record, write "no arrivals or departures on record since" the date the leadership entries were first seen, never "stable", "unchanged" or a span of years.
7. For up to 3 things you noticed, write: Seen (the count, the titles, the dates) | Consistent with (one reading, named as a reading) | Would confirm (what to check next).

If you have run this before for {COMPANY}, lead with what changed since then, and say "nothing new" in one line when nothing did. An earlier run is one you can see in this conversation or in memory your client provides: do not search files or folders for one. With none, say there is no earlier run, so this one is the baseline, and go on.

Rules: Keep every statement's grade: official means someone who speaks for one of the parties said it (check which party), reported means press or two independent sources, chatter means one unverified source and is never stated as fact. Give each fact the date it was last seen and its source address. An empty section is "not observed", never "none". A page can hold fewer entries than the limit asked for: read until `more` is empty. An open role is an intent to hire on a date, not a hire. Fewer open roles is not layoffs. Never give a reason for a departure unless it was stated. Roles, employers, dates and public statements only: nothing about anyone's private life. Answer from LMTY's record. Anything from outside it (a web search, a careers page you read yourself) goes only in a last section headed "From the assistant's own web search", with its link and the date read: never in a count, the mix or a signal.

playbooks.title: In Their Own Words
playbooks.when: On demand. Monthly if you're watching a company's messaging. A repeat run should lead with wording that changed.
playbooks.summary: Collect how a company describes itself, word for word: its headlines, category, proof points, and what its leaders say.
playbooks.delivers: Its wording by page, the category it claims, the evidence and figures it cites, how its wording has changed, and up to 10 dated quotes from its leaders. For a person: what they've said in public.

inputs.name: COMPANY
inputs.description: Company, product or person you want to quote

examples: How does Northwind describe itself?
What category does Initech say it's in now?
What was Northwind's homepage headline before the relaunch?
What proof points does Northwind use?
What has Northwind's CEO been saying lately?
What has Initech's founder said in public this year?
playbooks.playbook:
Show me how {COMPANY} describes itself, in its own words, and how that has changed.

Use the LMTY MCP tools. Its public profiles need no sign-in. If the tools are not available, say so and stop: the server is `https://mcp.lmty.com/mcp`.

1. Call search_profiles for "{COMPANY}". Read the company's profile and, when it has a main product, the product's. Say which words came from which.
2. Call get_profile with sections ["facts"] and factKinds ["tagline", "category_claim", "proof_point", "boilerplate", "page_meta", "milestone"]. Copy each wording exactly, with its page and the date last seen. Leave out button labels: stored as taglines, they are not messaging. A count of customers or users it claims can also sit under kind financial: look there before saying it cites none. The overview's `about` text is LMTY's writing: never quote it as the company's words. With no heading, tagline or category term on record, write "not observed in LMTY's sources" and move nothing else into that slot: wording read on the site or by search goes only in a last section, "From the assistant's own web search", with link and date.
3. Call get_profile with sections ["terms"] for the category terms its pages use and the earliest use known of each.
4. Call get_profile with sections ["statements"] for what its founders and executives said in public. Keep the speaker, the venue and the date. A statement graded official can be another company's leader speaking: check the speaker's employer. A statement by another company's leader about {COMPANY} is not its own words: leave it out and say in one line how many there are. A leader's remark that names no company (on the market, hiring, technology) is that person's: quote it under their name and role, and call it the company's position only if it is about the company's own product, customers or plans, or they say they speak for it.
5. A wording with an end date was replaced. Pair old and new only where they held the same page and heading, and give both dates. Wording first seen when the page was first read is not new wording. Give no reason for a change unless a source states one: write "no source states why".

If {COMPANY} is a person (search_profiles gives type person): do only step 4, on that person's profile, and write only their statements, newest first, and what the words do not show. Say which company they speak for, from their current roles, and that the company's own wording is a separate read. What others said about them is not their words: leave it out and count it. A person has no headline, tagline, category or boilerplate: leave those parts out, not empty.

Write: What it says it is (page, heading, line beneath, last seen) | The category it claims | The proof it cites | How the wording has moved | What its leaders say (up to 10 quotes, newest first) | Do the voices agree (its pages against its leaders) | What the words do not show.

Rules: Keep every statement's grade: official means someone who speaks for one of the parties said it (check which party), reported means press or two independent sources, chatter means one unverified source and is never stated as fact. Give each fact the date it was last seen and its source address. An empty section is "not observed", never "none". A page can hold fewer entries than the limit asked for: read until `more` is empty. Quote, never paraphrase; mark any summary as yours. A company's statement proves only that it said so. Describe a change in words ("'for small teams' no longer appears in the heading"), never as intent ("moving upmarket"). Do not tidy a spoken quote.

playbooks.title: Portfolio Brief
playbooks.when: Weekly or monthly for a list you're watching. A repeat run should start with developments dated since the last run, and say so when there's no earlier run to compare with.
playbooks.summary: Scan your list of companies for recent developments worth a look, with the evidence, dates, and one follow-up question for each.
playbooks.delivers: A line saying how much of your list it read. Then up to 8 companies with something worth following up on, each with the evidence, its date, and one question to ask. Every other company is listed with why it wasn't flagged: nothing dated, nothing that met what you asked, not read, or not identified.

inputs.name: COMPANIES
inputs.description: The list of companies to scan

inputs.name: CRITERION
inputs.description: What to look for

examples: Which of my portfolio companies need my attention this week? Northwind, Initech, and Globex.
Here are our 15 holdings. What should I follow up on this month?
Run the monthly watchlist brief on these 25 companies.
Which of these is in trouble: Northwind, Initech or Globex?
Anything new on my key accounts since last week's brief?
Give me follow-up questions for the board on each company in this list.
What are Initech Ventures' holdings, and which need attention?
playbooks.playbook:
Which of these companies merit my attention, and what should I follow up on? {COMPANIES}

What counts as needing attention: {CRITERION}. If I gave none, use this default and say so: funding, an acquisition or a sale, a leadership arrival, a price or plan change, a product launch or an end of life, a legal action, or a security incident, dated, in the last 90 days. Go by what an entry says, not its kind: an outage or a routine version release alone does not count; give releases as a count.

Use the LMTY MCP tools. Its public profiles need no sign-in. If the tools are not available, say so and stop: the server is `https://mcp.lmty.com/mcp`.

Work only from my list. Never look up a fund's holdings: ask for the list.

1. Call search_profiles for each of the first 30 names; name any beyond as not read. A name several profiles match: do not pick, put it under "Could not confirm". No match: search once more under the other obvious name, and show a profile found that way under both names.
2. For every company found, call get_calendar with profileType, profileId and a small limit: it gives `total`. The list runs earliest first: if there is more, read the 30 entries before `total` (read on if `more` > 0), and say "the newest N of M entries, back to [date]". If the search also returned a product under the same name, or one differing only by a suffix such as ".ai", read its calendar too and name both.
3. Group each entry by `startsAtBasis`: occurred is "on [date]", published is "reported on [date]", observed is first seen. A page reading (what a page no longer lists or now lists) is "no longer listed as of [date]", naming whose page, or "now lists", whatever its basis. Only occurred and published entries are developments. Several entries about one event are one, with the strongest basis and its earliest date.
4. For each company to be shown, take the entry's grade and sources from get_profile with sections ["timeline"] and limit 50 for the profile its `companies` names (search_profiles for that name if needed). If it is not on that page, write "grade not read".
5. Write:
   - Coverage, first: of how many given, how many were read in full, read in part, not read, and not found. Then the criterion and whose it is
   - Merits attention (at most 8 companies, by date, and say so): the development and who states it; its grade and date; the entry and criterion it met, nothing else; one follow-up question on what it leaves unstated. Say once that a report's date is not the event's
   - Dated entries, none met the criterion; Nothing dated on record: names, one line each
   - No longer listed: one line; one page's names at once are one item with a count. Never a loss
   - Not read; Could not confirm, with the question that settles each
   Every name appears in exactly one place.

If none meets the criterion, write the coverage and criterion lines, one sentence saying so, and the one-line sections.

If you ran this before for this list (in this conversation or your client's memory, not a file search), lead with entries dated after that run; if not, say there is no earlier run to compare with.

Rules: Keep every statement's grade; chatter means one unverified source, is never stated as fact and never alone flags a company. No ranking, score, verdict or advice on a holding. If I ask which is in trouble, say the record cannot say. No motive, no forecast, nothing from memory. An absence is "nothing dated on LMTY's record", never "nothing happened". Anything from outside LMTY goes only in a last section, "From the assistant's own web search", with link and date.

playbooks.title: Company Post Drafts
playbooks.when: Weekly for a company you post about, otherwise on demand. A repeat run should draft only from developments dated since the last run.
playbooks.summary: Draft a short post about one company's recent developments, with two or three angles and a source on every claim.
playbooks.delivers: Two or three angles, each with the developments behind it, and one draft for you to review, with a source after every claim. It also says how much it read, what it left out, and why.

inputs.name: COMPANY
inputs.description: The company to write about

inputs.name: DESTINATION
inputs.description: Where the post is going

inputs.name: AUDIENCE
inputs.description: Who the post is for

examples: What could we post about Northwind's recent developments?
Draft a LinkedIn post about Northwind's launch last week.
Give me two or three angles for a newsletter item on Initech's funding news.
Write a hot take on what Northwind just announced.
Anything worth posting about Globex this week?
Draft something short for X about Initech's price change.
playbooks.playbook:
What could I post about {COMPANY}'s recent developments? It is going to: {DESTINATION}. It is for: {AUDIENCE}.

Use the LMTY MCP tools. Its public profiles need no sign-in. If the tools are not available, say so and stop: the server is `https://mcp.lmty.com/mcp`.

At most 8 tool calls. One company at a time: if I named a market or several, ask which one.

1. Call search_profiles for "{COMPANY}". If several match, ask which.
2. Call get_calendar with profileType, profileId and a small limit: it gives `total`. The list runs earliest first: if there is more, read the 30 entries before `total` (read on if `more` > 0), and report "the newest N of M entries, back to [date]".
3. For grades and sources, call get_profile with sections ["timeline"] and limit 50 for the profile the entries' `companies` names, often the product (search_profiles for that name if needed). An entry not on that page is "grade not read".
4. Put every entry in one group, by its `startsAtBasis` or `atBasis`:
   - dated by when it happened (occurred)
   - dated by a report (published): write "reported on [date] by [source]"
   - first seen (observed), and any page reading (what a page now lists, now says or no longer lists): write "now lists" or "no longer listed as of [date]", never "new", a departure or a loss. Left out and counted
5. Merge reports of one story: it takes the strongest basis among its entries (occurred, then published, then observed) and the earliest date of that basis, never a source's date. Then set aside any story first dated before the last 90 days.
6. Keep what the company said apart from what others said: "{COMPANY} says" or "announced on [date]" for its own source, "reported on [date] by" for press.
7. Write:
   - Coverage: entries read of how many, and how many are in each group
   - Angles: 2 or 3, or 1 when the record supports 1. Each is one sentence with the entries behind it, leading with a story dated by when it happened or by a report: choose by what the story is and how well it is supported, then newest first, and say how you chose. If its grade was not read, say "grade not read" and write no draft from it unless I ask
   - Draft, for the first angle only: at most 120 words for a social post, 250 for a newsletter item, every claim followed by its source in brackets with the source's own date, or "date not given". First line: "Draft, for a person to review before it is posted. Nothing has been posted or sent." Where it needs my view, leave "[YOUR VIEW: ...]": never write my company in as fact. For a hot take, write the same draft and say the opinion is mine to add
   - Left out and why (with counts): first-seen entries, page readings, merged reports, entries graded chatter, entries announced as coming, older stories

If no story is dated by when it happened or by a report, write "Nothing on record carries a date of its own", list the first-seen entries as "now lists", count the page changes, and write no angles and no draft.

If you ran this before for {COMPANY} (in this conversation or your client's memory, never a file search), use only entries dated after that run, or say "nothing new". With none, say this run is the baseline.

Rules: Keep every statement's grade; chatter means one unverified source, is never stated as fact and is in no angle. No motive, forecast or superlative of your own, and no claim the sources do not make. Nothing from memory. Post or send nothing. Anything from outside LMTY goes only in a last section, "From the assistant's own web search", with its link and the date read.

inputs.name: PRODUCT
inputs.description: The product you want the pricing history for

examples: How has Northwind's pricing changed over the last year?
What did Northwind's Pro plan used to cost?
When did Initech drop its free tier?

playbooks.playbook:
Show me how {PRODUCT}'s prices and plans have changed.

Use the LMTY MCP tools. Its public profiles need no sign-in. If the tools are not available, say so and stop: the server is `https://mcp.lmty.com/mcp`.

1. Call search_profiles for "{PRODUCT}". Prices sit on the product's profile, not its maker's. When a company and a product share a name, read the product.
2. Call get_profile with sections ["overview", "pricing"]. The plans on sale now are the overview facts of kind pricing_plan. In `pricingHistory`, `changes` are dated moves with before and after values, and `ended` are plans no longer listed. Page with offset until `more` is empty.
3. Build a timeline, oldest first: the date, the move (new plan, price up, price down, plan retired, closed to new buyers, allowance changed, model changed), from what, to what, and the grade and source where the record gives them. A move with no source of its own is marked "from LMTY's price record" and takes the date it was observed. A move the record words as reported keeps "reportedly" in the move itself.
4. Say when the record begins, as two dates when they differ: the earliest dated entry, and the date the current plans were first read. Nothing before the earlier is known, and a plan first seen on the later was not introduced on it.
5. Facts of kind reported_price are what people say they pay. List them apart, with who said it and when. Never use one to correct a listed price. Posts in get_profile sections ["chatter"] are a second place a price may be mentioned, unverified: read them only when there are no reported_price facts or I ask. Before writing that the profile has no reported prices, say which of the two you read, with counts.
6. Describe the pattern in 2 to 4 sentences, each with a count and dates: how many moves in what period, which way the entry price and the top price went, and whether prices or allowances moved.

Write: On sale now (table) | Timeline (table) | No longer listed | What people report paying | The pattern | What the record does not show.

Rules: Keep every statement's grade: official means someone who speaks for one of the parties said it (check which party), reported means press or two independent sources, chatter means one unverified source and is never stated as fact. Give each fact the date it was last seen and its source address. An empty section is "not observed", never "none". A page can hold fewer entries than the limit asked for: read until `more` is empty. A listed price is what the page said on a date, not what anyone paid. Write "no longer listed as of", not "discontinued". Never say why a price changed unless the company said why. With no history on record, give the current list and say the record starts now. The price list and the timeline hold only what LMTY's record holds. A price or a move from outside it (a web search, a page you fetch) goes only in a last section headed "From the assistant's own web search", with its link and the date read: never a row in either, and never in place of a price on the record. Do not reconstruct past prices from memory or undated pages.

playbooks.title: Profile Check
playbooks.when: Monthly, and after any launch, rename or funding round. A repeat run should lead with findings fixed, findings still open and findings that are new.
playbooks.summary: Compare what an AI assistant says about your company with the public record, and see what to fix first.
playbooks.delivers: The assistant's unaided answer beside the record; facts for you to confirm; possible gaps, outdated facts, and conflicting claims; and a ranked list of suggested fixes with the page each belongs on.

inputs.name: COMPANY
inputs.description: Company, product or person (your own)

examples: What does AI say about Acme?
Audit our public profile. What's wrong or missing?
How does Acme look to a buyer who asks their assistant about us?
We changed our name in March. Has the public record caught up?
Check what's out there about me as a founder.
playbooks.playbook:
Check what is said about {COMPANY}, which is my own company.

Use the LMTY MCP tools. Its public profiles need no sign-in. If the tools are not available, say so first, give the unaided answer from step 1 below that, and stop: the server is `https://mcp.lmty.com/mcp`.

1. Before calling any tool, write 3 to 6 sentences answering "what is {COMPANY}?" from what you already know, with the facts you would state: what it does, where it is based, how big it is, who leads it, what it costs. If you know nothing, say exactly that. Keep this text unchanged, and label it as one assistant's answer on the date, written out, naming the assistant and model, not what "AI" says.
2. Call search_profiles for "{COMPANY}" and get_profile for the overview. No profile at all is the first finding: pass on the tool's hint and continue from web search, marked as your own research.
3. Set your unaided answer beside the record, statement by statement: where they agree, where they differ, and what you stated that the record does not hold. Say "the record does not hold it" only if you read every section with a count above 0; otherwise say "not in the sections read" and name them. Neither side is the truth; each difference is a question for me. A price or figure you remembered is your memory, not an old price on record.
4. Lay out every headline fact for me to confirm, with what the record says, its grade and "still true?". Mark the rows worth a second look: an old date, two values, a source that is not us.
5. Names and channels: the `name`, former_name facts, `website` and the overview's `channels` with each `role`, for the company and its main product. Keep apart "missing from LMTY's record" (not held, may exist; it keeps no alias list) and "missing from our own site" (only `endedBy` gone or a `removed` change). Ask me which other search matches and channels are ours.
6. Missing: for each section whose count is 0, say what a reader would expect there and both possible reasons, without choosing: LMTY has not read it, or our pages do not show it. Offer a check as a question ("does your site have a customers page?"); never say a page is missing. Customers sit on the product's profile: a company's count of 0 is not a gap until the product's was read.
7. List facts that may be out of date, and facts the record gives two values for. Put each conflict to me as a question; do not say which value is right.
8. List statements that rest on one unverified source, quoted with who and when, for me, not you, to sort into three bins: untrue and worth answering, true and uncomfortable, or harmless.
9. Fix first: up to 10 rows, ranked by how many readers each reaches and how wrong it leaves them: the change, where it belongs, who is misled, the effort.

If you have run this before for {COMPANY}, lead with findings fixed, still open and new. An earlier run is one you can see in this conversation or in memory your client provides: do not search files or folders for one. With none, say this run is the baseline and go on.

Rules: Keep every statement's grade: official means someone who speaks for one of the parties said it (check which party), reported means press or two independent sources, chatter means one unverified source and is never stated as fact. Give each fact the date it was last seen and its source address. An empty section is "not observed", never "none". A page can hold fewer entries than the limit asked for: read until `more` is empty. Never tell me a fact is wrong: tell me what the record says and where it came from. No score for the whole profile.

playbooks.title: Prospect Stack
playbooks.when: On demand, before the call it is for.
playbooks.summary: Find out which tools a prospect is publicly known to use, split into what to mention and what to ask on the call.
playbooks.delivers: A table of known tools with who says so and since when, each labeled Mention or Ask, and 3 to 5 questions for the call.

inputs.name: ACCOUNT
inputs.description: The company you are about to speak to

inputs.name: WE_SELL
inputs.description: Your product or category, so the relevant tools come first

examples: What tools does Globex use?
Is Globex already using Northwind?
I have a discovery call with Globex tomorrow. What's in their stack?
Which of our integration partners does Globex use?
Who's the incumbent at Globex for project tracking?
playbooks.playbook:
List the publicly evidenced tools for {ACCOUNT}. I sell: {WE_SELL}.

Use the LMTY MCP tools. Its public profiles need no sign-in. If the tools are not available, say so and stop: the server is `https://mcp.lmty.com/mcp`.

1. Call search_profiles for "{ACCOUNT}" and settle the company by its website. If two companies could be the one meant, ask which and wait: a stack for the wrong company is worse than none. If one matches and its profile has no website, do not guess one: give the stack for that match, say which profile you used and ask me to confirm it.
2. Call get_connections with focusType "company", the focusId, kinds ["customer_of", "uses"] and includeEnded true. Add the number of edges returned to offset and call again until `more` is 0.
3. An edge does not say how the use is known. For a product whose use matters to the call, read the evidence where it exists: get_profile on {ACCOUNT} with sections ["connections"], or on that product with sections ["customers"] for the entry about {ACCOUNT}. For the others write "how it is known: not read". Then say who makes the claim:
   - Shown by the account: found on its own site or code, or named in its own job ad
   - Said by both: only when the account itself says it uses the tool (its own page or code, or a quote from a named person there). A case study only the vendor published is the vendor's claim
   - Claimed by the vendor: a logo or a name on the vendor's page. An official grade here means the vendor said so, not that the account confirmed it
   - Reported: an article says so
4. Date each one: "since" only for a start a source states, otherwise "seen since", and always the date last seen.
5. Bin each: Mention (the account's own side shows it, seen in the last few months), Ask (vendor-claimed, reported, or not seen lately), or leave out (ended long ago). An item graded chatter, or marked "how it is known: not read", is an Ask: raise it as a question, and never write it as "also uses" or "is known to use".
6. Write 3 to 5 questions for the call, each tied to one item: confirm an "ask" item, find who owns a tool, learn when it renews, probe a category where nothing is observed.
7. If what I sell is a category and names no product, list no likely incumbents from integrates_with ties: an integration says two products connect, not that {ACCOUNT} uses either. Say so, give any such tie in one line as "connects with, use not evidenced", and make it a question.

Write the questions first, then the table, headed "Publicly evidenced tools" and never "its stack" or "the tools it uses" (product, maker, who makes the claim, evidence, since, last seen, bin), then what the list leaves out.

Rules: Keep every statement's grade: official means someone who speaks for one of the parties said it (check which party), reported means press or two independent sources, chatter means one unverified source and is never stated as fact. Give each fact the date it was last seen and its source address. An empty section is "not observed", never "none". A page can hold fewer entries than the limit asked for: read until `more` is empty. "Known to use" is the strongest phrase for one item, and only with who makes the claim beside it. Not listed is not "does not use": most tools leave no public trace. Do not decide from memory who competes with whom. Do not look up any individual at the account. Anything from outside LMTY (a web search, a fetched page or job ad) goes only in a last section, "From the assistant's own web search", with link and date read: never in the questions, the table or a bin.

playbooks.when: On demand, before a partnership, investment, or acquisition conversation.
playbooks.summary: Map who leads, funds, and partners with a company, who it competes with, and who says so.
playbooks.delivers: A company's leaders, investors and owners, partners, and competitors, each with who states it, since when, and whether it has ended.

inputs.name: COMPANY
inputs.description: Company, product or person at the center

examples: Who backs Northwind?
Who does Northwind partner and integrate with?
What has Initech acquired?
How are Northwind and Initech connected?
Who does Northwind say its competitors are?
playbooks.playbook:
Map who {COMPANY} is tied to and how.

Use the LMTY MCP tools. Its public profiles need no sign-in. If the tools are not available, say so and stop: the server is `https://mcp.lmty.com/mcp`.

1. Call search_profiles for "{COMPANY}". Investors and owners attach to the company, integrations usually to its product; read both when I ask about both.
2. Call get_connections with focusType and focusId, includeEnded true, and `kinds` narrowed to one group at a time:
   - People: founded, leads, board_member, advises
   - Money and ownership: invested_in, acquired, subsidiary_of
   - Working ties: partners_with, integrates_with
   - Rivals: competes_with
   Add the number of edges returned to offset and call again until `more` is 0. Say how many of each of these kinds exist and how many you read. Give no count for a kind you did not ask for, such as customers or employment.
3. Call get_profile with sections ["facts"] and factKinds ["funding_round", "valuation", "funding_total"]. Pair an investor with a round only where a source names that investor in that round; otherwise list investors and rounds separately, never paired by nearest date.
4. For every tie you show, say who states it. A get_connections edge carries a grade and a source count, not its sources or whether its `since` is a stated start: for those, call get_profile with sections ["connections"], which carries both. A partnership listed by one side only is that side's claim. An integration in a directory shows a connector exists. A competitor on a comparison page is who that company chose to be compared with. Edges of kind competes_with, integrates_with and partners_with are stored in an arbitrary order: their direction does not show who named the rival, listed the integration or announced the partnership. Compare each source's site with each party's. With no source read, write the tie as existing between the two, "stated by: not read".
5. Date each tie: "since" only for a start a source states, otherwise "seen since". Mark ended ties and how the end is known.

Write: In short (3 or 4 sentences) | People | Money and ownership | Working ties | Rivals | Ended ties | Not on the map (stakes, terms) | From the assistant's own web search (anything from outside LMTY, only here, with link and date). Show every tie that bears on the question with its grade: an unverified tie is shown, labeled unverified. For a kind with more than 10 ties, give the count for each grade, name a grade group of 3 or fewer in full, show a larger group's best-sourced few, and give the rest as a number, never as names; count ended ties separately. Leave out a section with nothing in it. The "Not on the map" line names each of the 4 groups with no tie: "not observed in LMTY's sources" if the kind was read and empty, "not read" if it was not asked for; never "not assessed", "none" or "has no". A profile with 3 ties or fewer gets its freshness line, those ties (both parties named, with grades) and that line, in about 150 words, and nothing else.

Rules: Keep every statement's grade: official means someone who speaks for one of the parties said it (check which party), reported means press or two independent sources, chatter means one unverified source and is never stated as fact. Give each fact the date it was last seen and its source address. An empty section is "not observed", never "none". A page can hold fewer entries than the limit asked for: read until `more` is empty. A tie is as strong as its weaker end. A shared investor or board member is a path, not an alliance. No motive for a deal unless a party stated one.

playbooks.title: Security Claims
playbooks.when: On demand, or quarterly for each vendor you review. A repeat run should start with anything LMTY spotted for the first time, or that's no longer listed, since the last run.
playbooks.summary: Check the public evidence of a vendor's security and compliance: the certifications it claims, reported incidents, and what to ask the vendor for.
playbooks.delivers: The certifications the vendor claims, where each claim comes from, and which details LMTY's sources don't show. Then any reported security incidents, each counted once, what has changed, and up to 6 questions to ask the vendor. It's a checklist of public evidence, not a security approval.

inputs.name: COMPANY
inputs.description: The company or product under review

inputs.name: PURPOSE
inputs.description: What the review is for

examples: What public evidence is there of Northwind's security and compliance?
We're reviewing Northwind as a vendor. Which certifications does it claim?
Has a breach or a security incident been reported about Initech?
Is Northwind SOC 2 compliant, yes or no?
Globex sent us a security questionnaire about Northwind. What is public on its security?
It's the quarterly vendor review. What changed in Northwind's security claims?
playbooks.playbook:
List the public evidence of {COMPANY}'s security and compliance. It is for: {PURPOSE}.

Use the LMTY MCP tools. Its public profiles need no sign-in. If the tools are not available, say so and stop: the server is `https://mcp.lmty.com/mcp`.

At most 8 tool calls.

1. Call search_profiles for "{COMPANY}". A certification can sit on the company's profile or its product's: take both. If the search returns one, the other is among its overview's closest relations. If several match, ask which.
2. Call get_profile for each: `factKinds` counts the certification facts and `counts` the timeline entries.
3. For each profile that counts any, call get_profile with sections ["facts"] and factKinds ["certification"]. A fact is a name, a grade and a source: add no type, year, auditor or scope. The kind also holds laws and frameworks (list them as stated claims, not certifications) and credentials people hold (list them apart, as held by staff). Two spellings stay two rows.
4. For each profile, call get_profile with sections ["timeline"] and limit 50. Pick by `kind` and `statement` the entries on a security incident, a certification no longer listed, or a certification or trust page first seen.
5. Write, in order:
   - Title and first line: a checklist of public evidence, not a security approval
   - Coverage: profiles read, facts read of how many, timeline entries read of how many
   - If I asked yes or no ("are they compliant?"): "The record cannot answer that", why, then what the record holds
   - Claims (at most 15): what is claimed, who states it, the page, the grade, last seen. Every row is "the vendor states", or the other party by name, never "is certified" or "is compliant". Say in one line what official and reported mean
   - One unverified source says: any claim graded chatter, apart, never in the table
   - Not on record for each claim: the report's date, the period covered, the scope, the auditor, an expiration date. Always listed
   - Incidents on record (at most 10): one row per incident, not per report, with every report as a source. Date it by `atBasis` (published is "reported on"); a merged row takes the strongest basis and its earliest date. Unsure if two are one: two rows, saying so. Outages filed as incidents: one line of their own, never called a breach
   - Changes (at most 8): "first seen on", never added or new, for a first sighting or a page that now lists a name; "no longer listed as of", never lost or revoked, when a page stopped listing a name (take the page from the entry's source, not its statement). If a fact and the timeline disagree, give both and say so; on one page, with the fact seen later, write "listed again as of"
   - What to ask the vendor for (at most 6), each tied to a row: the report itself, its date and scope, a bridge letter, an incident's post-mortem

With no certification fact and no security entry, write only what was read, that nothing is on LMTY's record, and what to ask the vendor for.

If you ran this before for {COMPANY} (in this conversation or your client's memory, never a file search), lead with what was first seen or is no longer listed since then. With none, say this run is the baseline.

Rules: Keep every statement's grade; chatter means one unverified source and is never stated as fact. Nothing from memory: no certification, framework, auditor or breach not on the record. An absence is "not on LMTY's record", never "has none" or "no breaches". No verdict, score or advice. Anything from outside LMTY goes only in a last section, "From the assistant's own web search", with link and date.

playbooks.title: Asset Audit
playbooks.when: Quarterly, and on demand after a large market change. A repeat run should lead with claims that changed standing since the last audit, matched by claim and asset, and the changes recorded since its date.
playbooks.summary: Check the competitive claims in your battlecards, decks or pages against current evidence, and see which to fix first.
playbooks.delivers: Each claim marked current, stale, unsupported, contradicted or unknown, with its source and date, ranked by who sees it and what it costs if acted on, and who should fix it.

inputs.name: ASSETS
inputs.description: Paste the battlecards, decks or pages to check, or give their public web addresses

inputs.name: APPROVED_FACTS
inputs.description: Your approved facts about your own product, such as prices, certifications and references. Without them, claims about your product are marked unknown
inputs.example: SOC 2 Type II since March 2026; Pro plan $12 per user

examples: Audit our competitive materials for stale claims.
Is our Northwind battlecard still accurate?
Find the weak competitive claims in this launch brief.
Which claims across our battlecards and comparison pages can we no longer support?
Northwind changed its pricing. What across our materials does that touch?
Check these three pages against what we know about Initech today.
playbooks.playbook:
Check the competitive claims in these assets against current evidence and list how each holds up. Rewrite nothing.

Assets: {ASSETS}
Approved facts about our product: {APPROVED_FACTS}

Use the LMTY MCP tools (`https://mcp.lmty.com/mcp`), signed in to my LMTY account. A sign-in request is not a lost connection: say once that this needs my account, and stop. This audits what I gave you, not every asset we have: say so in the first line.

1. Call list_products and list_competitors. List the material claims (a buyer or rep could act on them; framing is not a claim), one entry per claim with every asset it sits in. A claim that varies across assets is a finding.
2. For each competitor named: get_freshness for its own as-of date, get_report one section at a time for the claim's subject, get_evidence for source, confidence and dates. Confidence none is unknown.
3. For a price, plan, certification, customer or wording claim, and for a competitor I do not track: search_profiles, confirm by website, then get_profile with the sections the claim needs (overview for plans on sale, pricing for the price history, customers, facts for taglines and proof points). Where profile and report differ, give both with dates.
4. Mark each claim supported and current | supported but stale | unsupported | contradicted | unknown, with source and date. A figure behind a newer source is stale when the asset is older than the source. Unsupported only when a full list for its kind (approved claims, references, prices) is silent; a partial source that is silent means unknown. Claims about our product are unknown without approved facts, and contradicted, not unsupported, when the approved facts deny them. A supported claim whose only voice is the party it flatters is that party's own claim: say whose.
5. Always call get_report_changes with since at the oldest asset's date and limit 50, then the next page while nextCursor is not null, and get_market_feed with family "event" for each competitor. A report change is dated by when LMTY recorded it: write "recorded on". An event's date is the change's own only when atBasis is occurred; published is "reported on", observed "seen on". Several entries about one move are one change. With no change found, write "no dated change found between [date] and [date]", never "always weak".
6. Rank what needs attention by how many people see it and what acting on it costs, and say the order is your judgment. Name who should fix each.

Open with: read [n] of [m] assets; evidence checked for [n] of [m] competitors; changes read back to [date], [n] entries. Then a count by mark, the ranked claims (up to ten), the rest by mark, and one row per competitor with its as-of date.

If you have audited these assets before, lead with claims that changed standing since then, reading events with recordedSince from that date. With no earlier run in view, say this one is the baseline.

Rules: No mark is a guess: never "likely holds" or "probably true"; say what was checked and what would settle it. Nothing from memory: a competitor's price, plan, customer, certification or date comes only from a tool result, my material, or a page read now. A page read outside LMTY is marked as your own reading with its link and date read, never replaces a figure LMTY holds, and is never the only basis for stale or contradicted. Not found is "not on LMTY's record as of [date]", never "they have no" or "removed". A public post never supports a claim about customers or how many.

Write a first line saying what was read (my notes, which competitors, how many changes, as-of dates), then the prep.

Rules: The buyer's words outrank my notes about them. Nothing about the buyer, the competitor or past deals from memory. Not found is "not on LMTY's record" or "not observed, as of [date]", never "they don't have". An event's date by its atBasis: "reported on" for published, "seen on" for observed, never "new"; a report change "recorded on"; skip created changes. playbooks.title: Enablement Refresh
playbooks.when: On demand, when a change makes existing material wrong.
playbooks.summary: Update a battlecard or talk track after a competitor changes something, with proof and a date for every new line.
playbooks.delivers: The change and how its date is known, each claim in your card marked current, stale, unsupported or incomplete, new lines with their proof and date, and what can stay as it is.

inputs.name: ASSET
inputs.description: Paste the battlecard, talk track or deck section to update
inputs.example: Our Northwind talk track, pasted below

inputs.name: COMPETITOR
inputs.description: The competitor the asset is about, as you track it in LMTY

inputs.name: CHANGE
inputs.description: The change that prompted this, if you know it. Leave it empty to have recent changes checked
inputs.example: Northwind raised its Standard plan price

examples: Northwind changed its pricing. Update our talk track and battlecard.
What in our Initech enablement does this change make stale, and what should it say now?

Reps keep asking about Initech's new integration. Update the card so it answers that.
